The coordinates of the point A are (3, 1). A is reflected with respect to the x-axis to the point B. B is rotated clockwise about the origin through 90° to the point C. Find the x-coordinate of C.
A. -3
B. −1
C. 1
D. 3
Solution
Key Steps: Find the coordinates of B first, and  then find the coordinates of C.
Coordinates of B = (3, −1)
Coordinates of C = (−1, −3)
∴ The x-coordinate of C is −1.
∴ The answer is B.

The point P is translated rightwards by 6 units to point Q. If the coordinates of the reflection image of Q with respect to the x-axis are (–3, 5), then the coordinates of P are
A. (–9, –5).
B. (3, –5).
C. (3, 5).
D. (9, 5).
Solution
Key Steps: • By reflecting the point (–3, 5) with   respect to the x-axis, the point Q   can be obtained.
• By translating the point Q leftwards   by 6 units, the point P can be 
  obtained.
Coordinates of Q = (−3, −5) → •
Coordinates of P = (−3 – 6, −5) → •
= (–9, −5)
∴ The answer is A.
